Input lever: A. The hook (true, specific, tied to her)
L1 (worst): L1: states a fact not in the investor's record (invented deal, company, cheque, quote or connection), or has no line about the investor at all
L2: L2: only generic lines that could go to any investor ('climate is on your list of sectors', 'you invest at pre-seed')
L3: L3: true and specific (names a portfolio company, a deal, or a thesis point from the record) but not tied to her company
L4: L4: true, specific and tied to her company, but the tie is a stretch, or it describes a portfolio company's space without support in the record
L5 (best): L5: a named recent deal or a thesis point from the record, tied to her company in the same sentence; every fact appears in factsUsed under a field that exists

Input lever: B. Her story (her lines, nothing invented)
L1 (worst): L1: invents a credential, number or customer, or changes her words so the meaning changes
L2: L2: leaves out her one-liner, founder line or traction, or paraphrases them loosely
L3: L3: all her lines present but out of order, repeated, or with her facts re-worded
L4: L4: all her lines word for word, right order, small flow issue (two sentences saying the same thing)
L5 (best): L5: her lines word for word in order (hook, who she is, what the company does, traction, ask); nothing added she didn't say; reads as one person wrote it

Input lever: C. Ready to send (ask, length, tone)
L1 (worst): L1: no ask, a banned phrase, says or hints AI wrote it, or promises a meeting or return
L2: L2: ask has no amount or wrong stage, or subject is 8+ words, or body over 120 words
L3: L3: within limits but generic or flattering ('impressive', 'amazing'); would take more than 5 minutes to fix
L4: L4: within limits, clear ask with amount and stage, 1–2 small edits (under 2 minutes)
L5 (best): L5: subject under 8 words and specific; body 60–100 words; ask with ₹ amount and stage in lower case; plain warm Indian English; she would send it as is
